headline: Efficiency-focused algorithms replace dense computation in sequence analysis tools
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Algorithms
summary: Recent preprints report large runtime and memory gains for sequence and single-cell tools, including brisc completing a 10M-cell workflow in 3 minutes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is efficiency engineering for sequence-derived computation, with resource use reported alongside accuracy. LinearRaccess computes RNA accessibility in O(N) time via beam-pruned inside-outside dynamic programming, removing base-pair span limits. Hub labeling replaces dense all-pairs snarl distance matrices in the vg distance index, enabling exact distance queries on large human pangenome graphs. Zindex uses interleaved ZOR filters and color-preserving merging for compact, SIMD-accelerated colored sequence search. Hybrid RY-mers add damage-aware multi-context seeds to strobealign, improving aDNA alignment and running 4-6x faster than BWA-aln. brisc and the extended simpleaf target multithreaded, memory-frugal single-cell quantification. The read-mapper characterization supplies systems-level evidence, locating memory-bound functions. The problems differ; the shared method is replacing costly dense or approximate computation with structured representations or pruning.
